Subject: Initial redlines and a couple of questions on hosting modes

Hi Mina,

Thanks for sending the DPA draft — our legal team reviewed and attached a set of redlines (see Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.pdf). Two items popped up that we need explicit language on before we can move to execution:

1) Hosting-mode data flow: We need one clear paragraph that describes how data flows and which entities may access customer data under Redwood Dedicated (Redwood-managed dedicated GPU pools) vs Redwood Private (customer VPC / on-prem). Specifically: who can access persistent storage and audit logs in each mode?

2) Subprocessors & cross-border transfers: Your matrix lists several cloud infra subprocessors. We need an assurance clause for dedicated instances that log export and backup retention defaults can be restricted to the region and that hires of additional subprocessors will be pre-notified.

We also included a small CSV mapping expected data categories to storage residency requirements (attached). Can we get a short write-up (1–2 paragraphs) that we can show our Security/Privacy council? If both are acceptable, procurement will route to DocuSign.

Thanks,
Olivia

Hi Olivia — thanks for the redlines and the CSV mapping. Karthik (privacy counsel) and I reviewed; quick answers below and a plan to update the DPA text this afternoon.

1) Hosting-mode data access (short summary):
- Dedicated: customer data is stored on storage volumes tied to the customer's dedicated pool. Only the customer's dedicated service instances and Redwood runtime orchestrators in the assigned region have operational access. Redwood engineers do not access customer data except under documented, auditable break-glass procedures for operational emergencies; those actions generate audit logs retained per the table in the DPA.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): customer controls the compute and storage. Redwood's control-plane only receives metadata necessary for service orchestration (e.g., heartbeat, model version pointers). No persistent customer content is stored in Redwood-managed storage in the Private model unless explicitly configured and mutually agreed.

2) Subprocessors & cross-border: we will add: (a) a regional restriction default for backups and logs for Dedicated deployments; (b) a 30-day notice for additions to the subprocessor list unless the change is an urgent security fix, in which case we’ll notify within 7 days and provide mitigation details.

Plan: Karthik will propose precise language for both bullets and attach a redline (PDF) by EOD. After your confirmation we’ll send a prepared DocuSign envelope with the final DPA + SOW.

Mina

Subject: Proposed DPA redline: hosting-mode descriptions & subprocessor notice period

Attn: Olivia / Acme legal — attaching a targeted redline to the DPA. Key edits (excerpt):

- "Hosting modes and Data Access": 
  * For "Dedicated" deployments, Redwood and its subprocessors shall confine operational access to storage and logs to the infrastructure assigned to the customer's dedicated pool. Administrative access by Redwood personnel requires prior documented approval and is logged with tamper-evident audit trails retained for the period in Section 6.2.
  * For "Private" deployments (VPC or on-prem), Redwood's control plane will only process non-content metadata required for orchestration. Unless expressly configured, persistent customer content will not be written to Redwood-managed storage.

- "Subprocessor additions": Redwood will notify the customer of non-critical additions to the subprocessor list at least thirty (30) days prior to engagement. For emergency subprocessor changes necessary to remediate a security or availability incident, Redwood will notify the customer within seven (7) days and provide a post-action report.

I attached Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.pdf with tracked edits. If that aligns, I can fold the text into the DPA template and issue the DocuSign envelope.

Regards,

Olivia / Samuel — quick confirmations and next steps: 

A) Defaults: audit log retention = 90 days (configurable down to 30 days on Dedicated by request). Backup retention default = 30 days for transient model caches, 365 days for customer-requested snapshot backups (we will list both in the DPA table). I asked Engineering to add the retention table to the DPA template (redline attached).

B) KMS for Private-managed backups: yes. For Private (VPC) customers who elect managed backups, we support customer-managed KMS keys (bring-your-own-key). We will add explicit language and a short operational note about key rotation and access procedures.
